text: Babanango is a small town situated approximately 58 kilometers north-west of Melmoth in the KwaZulu-Natal Province of South Africa. It was founded in 1904 and derives its name from a nearby stream and mountain. The town is home to the Babanango Game Reserve, a recently established big five game reserve that has served as a conservation initiative uniting the local community. The origin of the name 'Babanango' is uncertain, with several theories proposed; the most commonly accepted version comes from the Zulu words 'baba nango'. A popular story recounts that many years ago a young Buthelezi child got lost on the slopes of a mist-shrouded hill and was found by an elder brother, who shouted, "baba, nango," meaning "Father, there he is." Nearby, eMakhosini lies in the Mkhumbane Valley along a tributary of the White Umfolozi River, close to Babanango, and was the site of King Dingane kaSenzangakhona's royal kraal, UmGungundlovu, where Piet Retief and his Voortrekkers were massacred in 1838. The name "Mgungundlovu" is believed to mean "the place of the elephant," while "eMakhosini" means "At the place of the chiefs." Babanango was originally part of a land grant given in 1885 by King Dinizulu to European farmers in recognition of their support following his father's death the previous year. The name Babanango also appears as the title of the song "Baba Nango" on Juluka's sixth album, Work For All.
